what: This is a preferred share of Microchip Technology, which makes microcontrollers and analogue chips used in cars, industrial machines and consumer devices. It pays a fixed dividend and ranks ahead of the ordinary shares.
customers: The company sells chips to industrial, automotive and consumer manufacturers; this security is held by investors seeking a fixed payment.
money: power management, interface and timing chips
moat: The underlying business has tens of thousands of customers whose products stay in production for a decade or more, which supports the earnings behind this dividend.
risks: The dividend is declared at the board's discretion
It ranks behind about $5.5 billion of the company's debt
The chip business went through a severe downturn, with revenue falling about 18% a year over three years
Its market price falls when long-term interest rates rise
opportunities: A yield well above the ordinary shares
Paid before ordinary shareholders receive anything
Revenue grew about 7% last year as the chip cycle turned
watch: The company's revenue recovery and continued declaration of the dividend.
